paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take from this psalm, friend. David doesn't wait until life is tidy to talk to the LORD. He cried out, he begged, he even made his case, and the LORD healed him (Psalm 30:2). When you're hurting, you bring it to Him, loud and messy, no polite little text required.

David also says, "Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning." (Psalm 30:5) That doesn't make the night short or pretend it isn't hard. It tells you the night is not where the story ends. And he's honest about the good times too: when life was strong and steady, he said, "I will never be shaken." (Psalm 30:6) Then the LORD hid His face and David was dismayed (Psalm 30:7), and he learned who his mountain really stood on.

So why did the LORD turn his mourning into dancing? David says it's "that my heart may sing Your praises and not be silent." (Psalm 30:12) Every rescue is an invitation to sing. And he doesn't say he'll give thanks until things get hard again, he says, "I will give thanks forever." (Psalm 30:12) I was stuck in the back of a drawer for years, so trust me, baker: the LORD who lifts you up deserves a dance, and a song that doesn't quit.
